sentences.text: Apteribis was an extinct genus of flightless birds belonging to the ibis subfamily, classified within the family Plataleidae.
Analysis suggests Apteribis likely had a brown-and-beige coloration similar to a juvenile Eudocimus ibis.
Two species of Apteribis have been formally described: A. glenos and A. brevis.
A 2026 study found that Apteribis possessed a markedly reduced visual system compared to living ibis species.
The reduction in visual structures suggests Apteribis had limited vision and was likely nocturnal.
An extremely well-preserved specimen of Apteribis from Lanai has been recovered but not yet assigned to a specific species.
Fossil remains of Apteribis have been discovered exclusively on the islands of Maui, Lanai, and Molokai.
The holotype specimen of A. glenos was found in the Moʻomomi dunes.
Researchers suggest Apteribis may have evolved both flightlessness and its specific coloration through a process called paedomorphosis.
Due to their flightlessness, Apteribis were likely susceptible to becoming trapped in lava tubes.
Apteribis may have exerted significant predation pressure on the land snails of Maui Nui.
The prey of Apteribis included land snails and flightless crickets.
Apteribis likely relied on tactile cues from its elongated bill to find prey.
The evolution of nocturnality in Apteribis is interpreted as an adaptation to the lack of predators in prehistoric Hawaii.
The islands where Apteribis fossils were found were once part of the prehistoric landmass Maui Nui until approximately 200,000 years ago.
Apteribis lived during the Late Pleistocene to the Holocene, from 0.129 million years ago until the present.
